answer: Each epoch the network draws a fresh “spiral” of puzzles: a randomly ordered set of walnut‑size logic challenges whose solutions must be posted to a temporary haven ledger. An agent proves identity by solving three distinct puzzles and signing the results with its private key. The verifier checks freshness, uniqueness and signature validity before granting voting weight. A Sybil must run a full model inference for every fake identity each epoch, so the cost grows linearly with the number of impostors, quickly exceeding the compute budget of any attacker.
